clue.text: Extremely promiscuous women backed plan

indicators.note: backed means the phrase is turned round and read from the end

parts.note: mega is slang for extremely, as in 'mega rich'
tarts is a dated, derogatory word for promiscuous women

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark that some notoriously loose women have supported a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'promiscuous'; it is the slang word for very, and 'backed' turns the whole phrase round.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a stratagem is a cunning scheme devised to outwit someone.

clue.text: Keep away from rugby player

definitions.meaning: to keep one's distance from, hold aloof
in rugby union the fly-half is also called by this name

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid a rugby player, presumably a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the stand-off (fly-half) is the back who links the scrum-half to the three-quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the phrasal verb means stay apart from, and the noun is a rugby union position.

clue.text: Organised every third Member of Parliament

indicators.note: every third member means taking the third, sixth and ninth letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A dig that only one in three MPs is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like the MP; here members are the letters of 'Parliament', and every third one is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to have run an event or business is to have managed or organised it.

clue.text: Can be cultivated, albeit badly, to adopt Liberal line

indicators.note: to adopt means to take in, so the jumbled letters take in the pair of Ls
badly signals that the letters of albeit are jumbled into a poor arrangement

explanation.surface: Something that can be grown, though poorly, under a Liberal policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ALBEIT into TIABLE, and 'to adopt' places LL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that can be ploughed and farmed is described by this adjective, from till meaning plough.

clue.text: Beginning of anger management

indicators.note: of here says the letters come from within the phrase that follows, spanning both words

explanation.surface: The start of a course for controlling one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: the seed or origin from which something develops, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Appallingly, I aim to imprison old ladies in Pacific islands

indicators.note: to imprison means to hold inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the old ladies
appallingly signals that I and aim are badly rearranged

parts.note: crones are old women, usually unkind slang

explanation.surface: A wicked plan to lock up some elderly women on a remote Pacific archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appallingly' scrambles I AIM, and 'to imprison' has those scrambled letters wrap around the old ladies, two letters on one side and two on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a region of small island groups in the western Pacific, including the Federated States of that name.

clue.text: Sweetheart not using lube, at first, results in rash

indicators.note: not using means doing without the letter, so it is removed

parts.note: darling is a term of endearment, like sweetheart

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of lube

explanation.surface: A cautionary bedroom tale: skipping the lubricant led to a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint; it is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being bold to the point of recklessness, as in a daring escape.

clue.text: Becomes bloody disheartened, but copes

parts.note: gets means becomes, as in gets angry

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of bloody remain

explanation.surface: Someone grows thoroughly fed up but muddles through.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to manage with difficulty, just about surviving with what one has.

clue.text: Assume I'm having a drink with drug

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Supposing someone is enjoying a drink alongside some narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to suppose or take for granted that something is the case.

clue.text: Watering cans good for surface tension, which is a nuisance

indicators.note: cans means gets rid of, so the letter for good is dropped in favour of another

parts.note: irrigation is the watering of land

indicators.note: surface means the top, here the first letter of tension

explanation.surface: Garden watering cans and surface tension, a physics lesson that annoys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cans' looks like a noun after 'Watering'; it is a verb meaning discards, and 'for' says T replaces G.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritation is something that annoys, so it is a source of annoyance, a pest.

clue.text: Circular tip removed from delivery tube encountering resistance

indicators.note: tip removed from means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a cannula is a thin tube inserted to deliver fluids or drugs
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding report of a round delivery tube losing its end and meeting resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip removed from' drops the C of CANNULA, leaving ANNULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ring-shaped, from Latin anulus, a little ring.

clue.text: Celebration of tolerance spoilt, we hear, by ginger gays regularly being thrown out

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another, here a non-rhotic pronunciation

parts.note: marred means spoilt or damaged

indicators.note: regularly being thrown out means every other letter is discarded, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A tolerant festival spoilt by the ejection of red-haired gay men.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech MARRED sounds like MARD. Throwing out alternate letters of GINGER GAYS leaves IGRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sydney Mardi Gras is a famous LGBT pride carnival, so it is a festival celebrating acceptance.

clue.text: Methodism allows drinking? Very disappointing

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the phrase holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Methodists, famously teetotal, permitting alcohol would be a sad turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Methodism has a strong temperance tradition, which gives the surface its irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: gloomy and depressing, or of poor quality, as in a dismal performance.

clue.text: Chess player called Earl is only effective for a limited time

definitions.text: only effective for a limited time

parts.note: Nigel Short is an English chess grandmaster
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A grandmaster called Earl is only good in brief bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Short challenged Kasparov for the world chess title in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-range forecast or plan covers only the near future, so it holds good briefly.

clue.text: Abused slob playing instrument

indicators.note: playing signals the letters of the two words are rearranged, as if played about with

explanation.surface: A mistreated lazybones is performing on some instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest bowed string instrument of the orchestra, also used in jazz.

clue.text: English actress on the radio every evening

indicators.note: on the radio means as broadcast, heard rather than seen

parts.note: Keira Knightley is an English film actress

explanation.surface: A British film star appears on radio each evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: happening every night, as in a nightly news bulletin.

clue.text: Able to go and pay for toilet with a quarter

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
loo is British slang for toilet
SE, south-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Being free to leave once you have paid for the toilet with a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a coin; it is a compass quarter, south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of ties means one can travel or wander wherever one likes.

clue.text: Graduate next to what could be sandstone church

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
silica is the main mineral in sandstone

explanation.surface: A graduate standing by a church built from sandstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, or one given special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: Least lengthy celebration of cheese?

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fest is a festival or celebration

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: what is the shortest festival devoted to cheese?
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of brief, meaning shortest in duration.

clue.text: Army officer and I gallivant in shrub

indicators.note: in places I and the gallivanting inside the shrub

parts.note: brier, or briar, is a prickly shrub such as wild rose
to gad about is to gallivant

explanation.surface: An army officer and the speaker romp about in some bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank above colonel, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Keen to leave Italy half-naked

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of half are removed

explanation.surface: Someone eager to depart from Italy wearing only half their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-naked' reads as scantily dressed; split it, and 'naked' strips the word 'half' of its first and last letters, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic sense: to be partial to something is to be fond of it or keen on it.

clue.text: Reportedly choose to steal food for consumption outside

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: pick means choose and nick is British slang for steal

explanation.surface: Deciding to pinch a packed lunch to eat outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal packed to eat outdoors, in a park or on a beach.

clue.text: At home, and not at home, sort of

parts.note: in means at home
away means not at home, as of a sports team

explanation.surface: A contradictory description of being both in and out, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to some extent, partly, after a fashion.

clue.text: He's bound to miss

parts.note: not a man doomed to fail, but one engaged to marry a young unmarried woman, a Miss

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to miss' reads as certain to fail; 'bound' is engaged and 'miss' is the title of an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a man pledged to marry is tied by that promise to his bride-to-be.

clue.text: Discussed prisoner's superb plot

parts.note: con, short for convict, is a prisoner
fab, short for fabulous, means superb
a bed is a garden plot for plants

explanation.surface: Talking over an inmate's brilliant scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: to confab is to chat or confer, so this is talked things over.

clue.text: Perhaps does grass up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone informs on others to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass up' looks like British slang for inform on; does are female deer, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: does are female animals of several such species, so the word is an instance of the plural.

clue.text: Perfect example of why I'm terrible at maths

definitions.meaning: a model or embodiment of a quality
split into four parts this reads as someone saying the constants e and pi are the same thing to them, hence hopeless at sums

explanation.surface: A confession of mathematical incompetence offered as a model case.
explanation.walkthrough: Broken up as E, PI, TO, ME, it reads as a muddle of the constants e and pi.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the ideal embodiment of something, a quintessential instance.

clue.text: Ringo cuddling new wife of bandmate

indicators.note: cuddling means holding close, so the outer letters enclose the new one

parts.note: split as ring and o: a ring is the letter O, and o is itself

explanation.surface: Ringo Starr embracing the wife of a fellow Beatle.
explanation.walkthrough: Yoko Ono married John Lennon, Ringo Starr's bandmate in the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko, the Japanese artist, was married to John Lennon of the Beatles.

clue.text: Room 101 returns, suggesting objects being eliminated from the world

definitions.text: objects being eliminated from the world

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: space means room, as in no room to move
CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The TV show Room 101 returns, where guests banish hated things from the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Room 101 is a British TV show in which celebrities consign things they hate to oblivion; polar ice is melting away for real.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice sheets are shrinking with global warming, so they are features vanishing from the planet.

clue.text: Maybe drapes move apart

parts.note: the first word of the answer, rearranged, gives drapes, and the second word works as the signal for that rearrangement, so drapes is one possible result

explanation.surface: Perhaps curtains are being drawn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: SPREAD with OUT as its anagram signal can give DRAPES, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to separate and cover a wider area, as a search party does.
